known_facts_book1: Emperor of all the Winkies, living in a magnificent tin castle, every bit of him tin and all his joints kept well oiled.
Carries a gleaming axe to prove he is a woodman, but seldom has cause to use it.
Has a very good mind but a heart he says is not of much account, so he is careful to do nothing unkind or to hurt anyone's feelings.
Says at the council that it is his duty to Ozma to go.
**Chops the passage through the palm barrier** with his axe, in a surprisingly short time, when the party reaches the Skeezers' lake.
Covers the ground on the march as easily as Uncle Henry and the Wizard, and shares a tent with the Scarecrow at the camp.

known_relations_book1.Ozma: The Ruler he owes a duty to.

not_in_this_book: the Tin Woodman fights the Flatheads
the Tin Woodman enters the Dome

hallucination_signals: the Tin Woodman goes under water

known_facts_book1: A copper man with machinery inside him, so cleverly constructed that he moves, speaks and thinks by **three separate clockworks**.
Is very reliable because he always does exactly what he is wound up to do, but is quite helpless whenever his machinery runs down.
Speaks in a jerky machine voice: 'We-will-have-to-go-there-any-how.'
Moves slowly on the march and the slightest obstruction in the road halts him until the others clear it away.
Has his machinery kept wound by Betsy and Trot in turns, and shares a tent with Professor Wogglebug.
Is one of the counsellors the three Adepts marvel at, for living and thinking and talking like other people.

known_relations_book1.Betsy Bobbin: One of the two girls who wind him.

not_in_this_book: Tik-Tok runs down and is abandoned

known_facts_book1: One of Ozma's oldest friends and her companion on many adventures, with a crude body of tree limbs jointed with wooden pegs and a ripe pumpkin for a head.
Grows a field of fine pumpkins each year and carves a fresh head ready before the old one spoils, never carving it quite the same way twice.
Is the only pumpkin-headed man alive in the Land of Oz.
Is wearing a newly made head when the expedition sets out.
Suggests at the council that they throw a rope around the sunken island and pull it ashore.
Walks awkwardly because walking jars his head around on his neck and sends him off in the wrong direction, until the Frogman takes his arm.

known_relations_book1.Ozma: His oldest friend, whom he goes to rescue.
known_relations_book1.the Frogman: Who takes his arm so he can follow the path.

not_in_this_book: Jack Pumpkinhead's head spoils on the journey

known_facts_book1: Shaggy from head to foot — hair and whiskers, clothes and shoes — but very kind and gentle and one of Ozma's most loyal supporters.
Says at the council that the easiest way is simply to raise the sunken island, and when Glinda asks how, admits he does not know, having never raised one.
Approves the Wizard's plan of going to the lake before the mountain.
Shares a tent with Jack Pumpkinhead, and watches the magic mirror over the Wizard's shoulder during the Button Bright rescue.

not_in_this_book: the Shaggy Man enters the Dome
the Shaggy Man raises the island

hallucination_signals: the Shaggy Man goes under water
the Shaggy Man raises the isle

known_facts_book1: A great frog as large as a man, noted for his wise sayings, who came to the Emerald City from the **Yip Country** and is a guest of honor.

Is perhaps the most splendidly dressed of Ozma's counsellors: velvet long-tailed coat, satin vest, finest silk trousers, diamond shoe buckles, gold-headed cane and a high silk hat, in every bright color at once.
Asks the one practical question at the council — how big is the lake, and how big is the island — and is told nobody knows.
Proposes sending the Glass Cat after Button Bright, since the beasts can do her no harm.
Wipes his eyes on a purple silk handkerchief when he thinks the boy is a goner.
Takes Jack Pumpkinhead's arm on the forest march so his head does not steer him wrong.

known_relations_book1.Jack Pumpkinhead: Whom he steers along the path.
known_relations_book1.the Glass Cat: Whom he proposes as the search party.

not_in_this_book: the Frogman finds Button Bright himself

known_facts_book1: Dorothy's own uncle and the best farmer in all Oz, living near the Emerald City with his wife Aunt Em.
Teaches the Oz people to grow the finest vegetables, fruits and grains, and keeps the Royal Storehouses well filled — which is why he is a counsellor.
Says simply, at the council, 'We all feel like that' about not staying away while Ozma is in danger.
Carries Glinda's wicker box of sorcery on the march and brings it to her for the magic mirror.
Cannot bear to think of his dear niece Dorothy being out there under water, and asks in a grave voice how it shall be done.
Helps Cap'n Bill push the stranded submarine back into the lake once the water level drops.

known_relations_book1.Dorothy: His niece, whom he goes to rescue.
known_relations_book1.Cap'n Bill: His tent-mate, who helps him launch the boat.

known_facts_book1: A one-legged sailor-man who came to the Land of Oz with Trot and was made welcome for his cleverness, honesty and good nature.
Wears a wooden leg to replace the one he lost, and is a great friend of all the children in Oz because he can whittle any sort of toy out of wood with his big jack-knife.
Is a member of Ozma's council and joins the rescue expedition.
Keeps up with the others on the march despite the wooden leg, and can walk as far as any of them.
Says only 'Comes of getting lost!' with a sigh when Button Bright appears in the magic mirror between a tiger and a wolf.
Shares a tent with Uncle Henry, and helps him push the submarine back into the lowered lake.

known_relations_book1.Trot: The girl he came to Oz with.

canonical_aliases_book1: Professor H. M. Wogglebug, T. E.
known_facts_book1: Head of Princess Ozma's Royal Athletic College; the 'H. M.' means Highly Magnified — he was once a little bug magnified to the size of a man and always remained so — and 'T. E.' means Thoroughly Educated.

Invented the **Educational Pills**: a Geography Pill after breakfast teaches the whole geography lesson in an instant, a Spelling Pill the spelling lesson, an Arithmetic Pill any kind of sum without thinking about it.
Made the college very popular with these pills, which save the students from studying and leave all their time for football, baseball and the like.
Is **not a favorite outside his own college**: he is so conceited and displays his cleverness and learning so constantly that no one cares to associate with him.
Is nonetheless of value in Ozma's councils, where he proposes that they all get under the sunken island and lift it — and is asked how they would get under it.
Shares a tent with Tik-Tok at the camp.

known_relations_book1.Ozma: The Ruler whose Athletic College he heads.
